hypotheses.statement:
For every integer $r\ge4$ there are constants $C_r>0$ and $\Delta_r\ge3$ such that every $K_r$-free graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta\ge\Delta_r$ satisfies $$\chi_{\mathrm{DP}}(G)
 \le \left\lceil C_r\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\right\rceil.$$ The constants depend only on $r$.

For every finite graph $F$ there are constants $C_F>0$ and $\Delta_F\ge3$ such that every $F$-free graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta\ge\Delta_F$ satisfies $$\chi_{\mathrm{DP}}(G)
 \le \left\lceil C_F\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\right\rceil.$$

For every integer $r\ge4$ there are constants $A=A(r)>0$, $B=B(r)\ge1$, and $\Lambda_r\ge1$ with the following property. Let $\Lambda\ge\Lambda_r$, and let $H$ be a finite $K_r$-free graph whose vertex set has a partition $\mathcal D$ such that each vertex has at most one neighbor in each part. For any positive vertex weights with $s_i\le\Lambda$, there is a finite family of the multiplier and drop operations defined above, with vectors $g^{(j)}$, listed supports $J_j$, and rates $a_j\ge0$, such that $$\label{eq:adjustment}
 t_i+\sum_j a_jg_i^{(j)}\le B d_i,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j:\,i\in J_j}a_j\le\Lambda^4
 \qquad(i\in V(H)).$$ The constants depend only on $r$.

For every integer $r\ge2$ there is a constant $D_r\ge1$ such that the following holds. Let $F$ be a finite $K_r$-free graph with positive vertex weights $q_i$ of total mass $s$. For every $0<\epsilon\le1/2$, there are jointly distributed random multipliers $n_i$ satisfying $$\label{eq:sparse-multipliers}
 0\le n_i\le D_r\epsilon^{-(r-2)},\qquad
 \mathbb En_i=1,\qquad
 \mathbb E\sum_{iu\in E(F)}q_iq_u n_i n_u\le\epsilon s^2,$$ where the edge sum is unordered.

Let $F$ be a graph with a homomorphism $p:F\to H_b$ that is injective on directed edges. Give every vertex of $F$ the weight, prices, coefficients, and part of its image. Then every vertex of $F$ has at most one neighbor in each inherited part. Moreover, [eq:local-cross] holds in $F$ for any $S,D\subseteq V(F)$ satisfying the mass and coefficient hypotheses of Lemma 5, provided $S\cup D$ lies in a ball of radius $R_0$ in $F$ and meets each inherited part in at most $P_0$ vertices.

For the graphs $H_b$, weights $q$, and prices constructed above from [eq:dual-test], with $A$ chosen as in Lemma 5, the quantities in [eq:price-mass] and [eq:dyadic-triangle-mass] satisfy $$T_0\le O_r(M_x).$$ The implicit constant depends only on $r$.

Let $32\le\ell\le\ell_0$, and let $F$ be a nonempty finite graph with no isolated vertices, with a homomorphism into some $H_b$ injective on directed edges. Give its vertices the inherited weights, prices, and parts, and suppose that [eq:prepared-level] holds. There is a graph $F'$ obtained by splitting vertices and retaining at most one copy of each edge of $F$, with unchanged vertex weights, such that every neighborhood of $F'$ has weight at most $e^{\sqrt\ell}$ and $$\sum_{\{a,u,v\}\text{ a triangle of }F'}q_aq_uq_v \ge \left(1-C_2\frac{\log\ell}{\sqrt\ell}\right) \sum_{\{a,u,v\}\text{ a triangle of }F}q_aq_uq_v, \label{eq:split-retention}$$ where $C_2$ depends only on $r$. The projection $F'\to F$ is a homomorphism injective on directed edges.

With the above definitions, $$H_0\ge-\log\ell,\qquad H_R\le O_r(\log\ell).
 \label{eq:walk-entropy-bound}$$

Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be bounded real functions of finitely many independent inputs. Suppose that $X_j$ has range of length at most $b_j$, and that each input is used by at most $p$ of the functions, where $p\ge1$ is real. If $\sum_jb_j^2>0$, then for every $a>0$, $$\label{eq:input-concentration}
 \mathbb P\left(\sum_j(X_j-\mathbb EX_j)\ge a\right),\quad
 \mathbb P\left(\sum_j(X_j-\mathbb EX_j)\le-a\right)
 \ \le\ \exp\left(-\frac{2a^2}{p\sum_jb_j^2}\right).$$ If $\sum_jb_j^2=0$, both probabilities are zero.

purpose: Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique

coverage.checked_domain: Empty and isolated graphs; all partial matchings between two two-entry lists; all labeled simple graphs on three vertices with three-entry lists and empty or full edge matchings; invalid-contract boundary inputs.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exhaustive Cartesian-product enumeration of every entry assignment, followed by exact forbidden-pair checks; no candidate code is imported.

coverage.checked_domain: Disjointness, nonempty lists, endpoint membership, repeated matching endpoints, duplicate edges, loops, insufficient list sizes.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent graph construction and pairwise matching-relation checks. The oracle rejects wrong expected classifications and empty outputs.
